chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Mansur from the freedman of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
He said: 'The two rak'ahs of the Witr prayer, if he wishes, he may speak between them and between the third, and if he wishes, he may not separate (by speaking).'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And it is recommended that a person supplicate in the Witr with this supplication, and he mentioned the supplication until its end, to his saying: 'Then he prays the two rak'ahs of Fajr.' We did not concern ourselves with extracting the chains of narration for the supplication because concerning ourselves with other matters is preferable, and whoever wishes to rely on the supplication itself, let him take it from the book and from what has come regarding the encouragement to supplicate in the Witr.

key_terms.رَكْعَتَا اَلْوَتْرِ: The two rak'ahs of the Witr prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on speaking during the Witr prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility in the Witr prayer structure, permitting speech between the first two rak'ahs and the third, or combining them without interruption. Shaykh al-Tusi highlights the recommendation of a specific supplication, noting that while he omits its full chain of transmission to prioritize other matters, the text itself serves as a strong encouragement for devotion in this prayer.
